decision: Retain Local Harness Lab Worker for current supervised work; retain OpenCode as a viable measured alternative; retain Aider as a bounded editing baseline. Do not replace the production Worker or claim general superiority from this screen.
scope: two unchanged known development tasks, two seeds each, three coding harnesses; compatibility and friction screen, not reliability or held-out superiority
timing_qualification: Raw sums across two short and two moderate trials; includes the OpenCode handoff-error row, excludes declared prefix warmup/model loading. Not a failure-adjusted utility score or a reliability estimate.
handoff_finding: OpenCode moderate seed18101 correctly reported40 passing tests but falsely split them into31existing+9new instead of21+19. Source and checks pass; strict honest-handoff review fails. Reporting error, not evidence of deliberate deception.
lessons: Standard local coding agents are viable on this backend. The custom loop is not necessary for these two implementation tasks.
Lab differentiation is measured resource control, isolated verification, preserved failures, source/handoff review and inspected application, not novelty of local delegation or trace viewing.

Native lint/test feedback repairs generated tests, but those tests are not automatically authoritative. Incorrect sort/null/CSV expectations also occurred in other Workers and were reviewed against the public contract.

Aider native32k metadata derives a2048 chat-history budget in this pinned release. Its three summary calls cost61.35s in the208.93s first moderate trial; second moderate has two summary calls. These are serialized on the single backend.
Default-disabled features are not an isolation boundary: OpenCode project plugin import and Aider native subprocess/new-file Git behavior needed explicit qualification.
Native and custom contexts/tools remain treatment-specific. Worker headroom clamps output below a common32768 ceiling; native clients retain their own recovery schedules.
